subject: SDK examples refresh — scope, deadlines, and parity expectations (streaming/tools/structured output)
related_links: Confluence: Canonical patterns draft — Streaming + Tool Calling + Structured Output (DevEx)
body:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ibrahim Khan <ibrahim.khan@redwoodinference.com>, Dana Lo <dana.lo@redwoodinference.com>, Mateusz Zielinski <mateusz.zielinski@redwoodinference.com>, Sabrina James <sabrina.james@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 15, 2026 at 9:12 AM
Subject: SDK examples refresh — scope, deadlines, and parity expectations (streaming/tools/structured output)

Team — kicking off the cross-SDK + docs refresh for streaming, tool calling, and structured output examples.

Primary goals (high-level):
- One canonical conceptual flow across Python/TS/Go for:
  1) token streaming (including final response capture)
  2) tool calling (single + parallel tools, with partial arg deltas)
  3) schema-based structured output (validate + retry strategy)
- Minimize drift going forward via snippet tests/CI.

Scope + expectations:
- Examples must be copy/paste runnable with minimal deps and explicit setup.
- Maintain backward compatibility where possible. If not possible, the example must call out required SDK version.
- Avoid insecure patterns (no open-ended tool execution; no logging secrets; validate tool args).

Timeline (target 4–6 weeks; but we should ship updated examples + docs in ~4):
- Week 1 (this week/early next): audit + align on canonical event model + naming
- Weeks 2–3: land SDK example updates + docs updates + redwood-examples refresh
- Week 4: CI snippet tests green in SDK repos + docs deploy + release notes

Working links:
- Linear epic (inventory + owners): ENG-2841
- Canonical event model task: ENG-2842
- Canonical patterns draft (Confluence): “Streaming + Tool Calling + Structured Output — Canonical Patterns” (DevEx space)

Ask:
1) Please reply by EOD Fri with:
   - your proposed owner for each SDK + a backup reviewer
   - any known gotchas/SDK-specific constraints we need to reflect in docs
   - estimate for landing runnable examples + minimal tests
2) Ibrahim — please schedule a 30-min alignment early next week to lock event taxonomy + terminology.

Thanks,
Monica

—
Monica Patel
Exec Owner, SDK Engineering
Redwood Inference


From: Ibrahim Khan <ibrahim.khan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dana Lo <dana.lo@redwoodinference.com>, Mateusz Zielinski <mateusz.zielinski@redwoodinference.com>, Sabrina James <sabrina.james@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 15, 2026 at 10:03 AM
Subject: Re: SDK examples refresh — scope, deadlines, and parity expectations (streaming/tools/structured output)

Sounds good.

I’ll run the alignment meeting. Proposal for agenda:
- Stream event taxonomy: token deltas vs tool-call deltas vs final response object
- Tool call arg accumulation rules + what we consider “incomplete”
- Structured output: schema transport + validation + retry conditions (parse failure vs schema mismatch)
- Terminology: “tool calling” vs “function calling”, “structured output” vs “JSON mode”

I’ll send a calendar hold for Tue 10:30–11:00 PT.

Re: docs, I’d like to lock the canonical event naming in the Confluence draft first so the SDK + docs match.

- Ibrahim


From: Dana Lo <dana.lo@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ibrahim Khan <ibrahim.khan@redwoodinference.com>, Mateusz Zielinski <mateusz.zielinski@redwoodinference.com>, Sabrina James <sabrina.james@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 15, 2026 at 11:21 AM
Subject: Re: SDK examples refresh — scope, deadlines, and parity expectations (streaming/tools/structured output)

Owner/backup for TS:
- Owner: me
- Backup reviewer: Sabrina (if she has cycles), otherwise Ibrahim

TS gotchas to flag:
- AbortSignal vs timeouts: our examples need to show how to cancel streaming cleanly.
- Tool call deltas: we’ve had folks try to JSON.parse partial arg chunks. We should show explicit aggregation and only parse at completion.
- Parallel tools: we should add a concurrency limit in the sample to avoid people “Promise.all” on unbounded tool fanout.

Estimate:
- Streaming + tool calling runnable snippets: 2–3 days
- Structured output w/ Zod validation + retry guidance: 2 days
- Snippet tests: 1 day (depending on runner shape)

I’m aligned with locking naming in Confluence first.

Dana


From: Mateusz Zielinski <mateusz.zielinski@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ibrahim Khan <ibrahim.khan@redwoodinference.com>, Dana Lo <dana.lo@redwoodinference.com>, Sabrina James <sabrina.james@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 15, 2026 at 12:08 PM
Subject: Re: SDK examples refresh — scope, deadlines, and parity expectations (streaming/tools/structured output)

Go owner/backup:
- Owner: me
- Backup reviewer: Ibrahim

Constraints/gotchas:
- Context cancellation + deadlines are the standard way Go users will handle timeouts. We should show it in every streaming example.
- Scanner/read loop needs to handle mid-stream disconnect with a clear error and not silently drop the final chunk.
- Tool arg deltas: same as TS; don’t attempt to unmarshal until complete. We should store raw bytes/strings and validate once final.

Estimate:
- Streaming + tools: 3 days (includes tests for aggregation)
- Structured output w/ schema validation + retry: 2 days

Mateusz


From: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ibrahim Khan <ibrahim.khan@redwoodinference.com>, Dana Lo <dana.lo@redwoodinference.com>, Mateusz Zielinski <mateusz.zielinski@redwoodinference.com>, Sabrina James <sabrina.james@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 15, 2026 at 2:36 PM
Subject: Re: SDK examples refresh — scope, deadlines, and parity expectations (streaming/tools/structured output)

Adding docs POV:

If we can lock the canonical terminology and event semantics early next week, I can schedule the docs-site rewrite in parallel.

One request: please keep the “canonical patterns” doc prescriptive (Do/Don’t). In particular:
- Clear statement that streaming responses require handling a final response object (users keep missing this)
- Explicit warning on partial tool args + “only parse when complete”
- Structured output: recommend strict validation by default + what error to show when schema mismatch happens

Connor — when you have a sense of version bumps, I’ll align the docs deploy timing with SDK releases so we’re not publishing snippets that require unreleased versions.

Elliot


From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ibrahim Khan <ibrahim.khan@redwoodinference.com>, Dana Lo <dana.lo@redwoodinference.com>, Mateusz Zielinski <mateusz.zielinski@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sabrina James <sabrina.james@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jan 16, 2026 at 2:37 PM
Subject: Re: SDK examples refresh — scope, deadlines, and parity expectations (streaming/tools/structured output)

Thanks all — this is the right shape.

Decisions / expectations (so we’re aligned):
- Naming: user-facing docs will use “tool calling” and “structured output”. If we reference “function calling” / “JSON mode”, it’s only as “aka” for migration context.
- Stream examples must demonstrate:
  - consuming token deltas
  - aggregating tool-call deltas when present
  - capturing a final response object and handling errors
- Tool calling examples must:
  - use an allowlist/tool registry
  - validate and/or type-check tool args
  - explicitly show partial-args behavior and safe accumulation
- Structured output examples must include:
  - JSON schema definition
  - validation step
  - retry strategy for parse/validation failure (bounded retries)

Deadlines (to keep this moving):
- By Tue (after Ibrahim’s meeting): canonical event model + naming locked in Confluence and linked from ENG-2842
- By end of Week 2: runnable examples in each SDK repo behind snippet tests (even if minimal)
- By end of Week 3: docs-site PRs ready + redwood-examples PR(s) ready for review

Connor — please propose a release plan once we have a rough cut of the SDK PRs (patch releases are fine; priority is that docs reference released versions).

I’ll track status in the Linear epic (ENG-2841) and use it for weekly check-ins.

Monica

—
Monica Patel
Exec Owner, SDK Engineering
Redwood Inference
